analysis.lean: No real edge on the side or total; Boston is the clear better team but the -11.5 spread already prices that in.
why: Blended projection is BOS +11.6 against a -11.5 line, a 0.1 point gap, so the spread is priced correctly.
Blended total is 221.6 against 221.5, which gives no lean on the over or under.
Opponent-adjusted net rating is BOS +4.9 against BKN -6.5, a gap of about 11 per 100 possessions. BKN allowed 123.7 per game raw, but that is 3 games and is shrunk toward average.
Shot-quality matchup favors Boston: expected points per shot are BOS 1.174 and BKN 0.999 (league 1.084). That fits the margin but is already in the ratings.
BOS is on a back-to-back and BKN is on the third game in four nights. The packet counts neither as proven, so I did not adjust for them.
risks: Back-to-back for Boston raises blowout and garbage-time risk. Starters could sit late in a big lead, which would help the underdog cover.
Samples are 3 games per team. BKN's 0.607 opponent eFG and BOS's 134-99 win are likely to regress.
Brooklyn's only listed absence is Bilodeau, and Boston's is Carter (mono). Neither is a core rotation player, but the listed rotations show no other injuries, so check for late news.
matchups: Both teams take a high share of threes (BKN 45%, BOS 47%) and both defenses allow 50%, which means more variance on makes and misses. Treat this as context only.
BOS defense allows centers +17% threes per minute, a small sample for Sharpe and Clowney, so I would not move anything on it.
verify: Confirm Tatum and George are active on the second night of a back-to-back, with no load management.
Check the final injury report for Brooklyn (Randle, Porter Jr.) before tip.
Shop the spread: -11.5 against -12 matters when the model sits right at the number.

judgment.why: Our margin (+11.6 blended) sits almost on the -11.5 line and the total (221.6) on 221.5, so there is no edge beyond the market's fair price, and a 3-game sample is thin.

analysis.lean: Slight lean to Detroit +4.0, but the edge is thin and this is close to a pass.
why: Our raw projection has NYK at -1.3 and the market blend gives home +3.0, which is about a point shorter than the posted -4.0.
Detroit's opponent-adjusted net is 5.7 per 100 vs New York's 1.1. Detroit is 3-0 with a raw 118.3 scored / 105.7 allowed, and New York is 0-3 at 101.7 scored / 108.0 allowed.
New York's offense is weak so far (eFG 0.476). Detroit is strong on offense (eFG 0.563, ORB% 0.323), though Duren's absence is already priced into the projection (+1.2 margin).
Total: our 220.1 and the blended 218.8 are both within about 1.6 of the posted 218.5. Pace is 103.7 vs 101.9, so there is no clear total edge.

Matchup expected points per shot is DET 1.072 vs NYK 1.040, with the league at 1.084. Both defenses limit centers (DET -15% points, NYK -10%), which hurts New York's Towns more than Detroit's replacement bigs.
risks: Samples are only 3 games each, and New York's 0-3 start with a low-scoring offense may be noise. Brunson, Towns, Anunoby, Hart and Bridges are all healthy.
Ausar Thompson (ankle) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are both questionable for Detroit. Thompson plays 26 min and Joe 13.7 min, so their status shifts the rotation.
The track record is 12-13 over 25 picks, which is too small to lean on.
matchups: Detroit takes 43% of its shots from three and NYK allows 46%, above the league's 42%. NYK also allows forwards +11% threes, which helps Detroit's shooters like Robinson (5.0 3PM per game).
Detroit's guard defense allows -14% assists and -9% threes, which could limit Brunson's creation and Kolek's passing.

analysis.lean: No edge on the side or total; Spurs -17.5 and 230.5 are priced about right, so this is a pass or a very small lean at most.
why: The ratings projection is only +11.9 for SAS against a -17.5 market. Blended at weight 0.18 it lands at +16.5, so the market is carrying most of the number.
SAS is 3.6 net per 100 against SAC at -5.9 per 100, but both samples are only 3 games and shrunk toward average, which keeps the rating gap modest.

SAC's defense is poor: it allowed 124.0 per game raw, a 0.559 eFG against, and a 0.316 offensive rebound rate to opponents. The matchup expected points per shot is 1.146 for SAS against 1.023 for SAC, which favors SAS.
The projected total of 230.6 is almost identical to the posted 230.5. Pace is similar (SAC 103.8, SAS 104.3), so nothing points to a total edge.
SAS has 2 days of rest against SAC's 1 day and two time zones crossed. The projection counts these as worth nothing, so I add nothing.
risks: A -17.5 spread leaves room for garbage-time backdoor covers if SAS starters sit in a blowout.
All ratings come from 3 games per team, so the numbers could move a lot with more data.
SAS lost to HOU and OKC at home and shot only 0.507 eFG, so their offense is not yet proven.
matchups: SAC allows centers +8% points per minute, which fits a Wembanyama scoring night. Wembanyama averages 20.0 points and 11.0 rebounds so far.
SAC takes only 34% of its shots from three and SAS allows 32% of opponent shots from three (league 42%), so SAC's shot profile runs into a defense that gives up few threes.
verify: The injury report lists Keegan Murray as Out, but the projection credits SAC with +0.7 points for Murray playing (80% of recent games). If he is out, SAC is about 0.7 weaker than the model shows. The market likely already prices that, so I made no adjustment.

judgment.why: The market's fair prices (home wins 0.941, cover 0.507, over 0.499) already match the blended projection (+16.5 margin, 230.5 total), and I see no concrete reason to move off them.
